text:
Hiro: Hey folks, day 1 here — trying to get devbox parity between my M1 Mac and a Linux VM. Followed the bootstrap (asdf + brew + direnv) but running into three weird things: 1) asdf python builds on mac omit _ssl on import, 2) my fish shell doesn't pick up asdf shims in GUI apps, and 3) git pushes to our internal host keep prompting for a password (should be key auth). Anyone able to help debug quickly?

Sana: Welcome Hiro! :wave: Quick wins: for (1) check openssl version used at build time; for (2) GUI apps often don't get your shell env; for (3) check ssh-agent + ~/.ssh/config. Can you paste short errors?

Hiro: For python: `import ssl` raises ModuleNotFoundError: _ssl. asdf install log shows `configure: error: OpenSSL not found` even though brew lists openssl. I tried `brew install openssl@1.1` and set flags but build still fails.

Marcel: On Apple silicon brew is keg-only for openssl. Try:```bash
brew install openssl@1.1 readline xz
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
# clean build env to avoid Nix interference
env -i PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS" CPPFLAGS="$CPPFLAGS" asdf install python 3.11.4
```
That usually gets the ssl module built. Also check you don't have PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS that disable ensurepip.

Hiro: Did that in a fresh terminal, build succeeded and `import ssl` works. Thanks! That leaves fish + GUI apps. I use iTerm and also open VS Code from spotlight; VS Code launched from dock doesn't see `~/.config/fish/config.fish` envs so asdf shims show system python.

Sana: That's expected — mac GUI apps started from the Dock/Spotlight don't inherit your shellrc. Two options: 1) move minimal PATH exports and asdf init into `.zshenv` (if you use zsh) so login & GUI shells pick it up, or 2) always launch GUI editors from a terminal: `open -a "Visual Studio Code" --args .` or `code .` launched from terminal. For fish, add `set -x PATH $HOME/.asdf/bin $PATH` in `config.fish` and ensure VS Code uses a login shell for integrated terminal.

Hiro: I'm using fish as primary shell. Where should I put asdf init so both terminal and GUI processes see it?

Marcel: Best practice: put PATH prep in `.zshenv` or `.profile` because those are read by GUI login shells on mac. If you stick with fish, add a tiny shim in `~/.zshenv` that sets PATH and sources asdf, then have fish inherit it. Example `.zshenv`: `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"; . "$HOME/.asdf/libexec/asdf.sh"` — then GUI-launched apps get correct PATH. Terminal fish can still source `asdf.fish` for completions.

Hiro: Ok added `.zshenv` with that snippet and relaunched VS Code from dock — now the integrated terminal's `which python` points to `~/.asdf/shims/python`. Nice. Last blocker: pushing to git.internal.redwood.ai asks for password. `ssh -T git@git.internal.redwood.ai` shows `Permission denied (publickey)`. My SSH key is added to 1Password and I thought the 1Password SSH agent was running.

Sana: Two quick checks: `ssh-add -l` (does it list your key?) and `ssh -vT git@git.internal.redwood.ai` for debug. If you use 1Password, ensure the CLI is unlocked `eval $(op signin)` and the ssh agent is enabled per 1Password docs. Also confirm your key is uploaded to your account on the git host.

Hiro: `ssh-add -l` returns no identities. I ran `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and now `ssh -T` returns a welcome banner. Pushing works. Not sure why 1Password agent didn't add it automatically.

Marcel: If you rely on 1Password, add `eval $(op signin)` to your login scripts and enable the 1Password SSH agent so keys are loaded at unlock. Many folks still prefer `ssh-add` in `~/.profile` for simplicity.

Hiro: All green now. I pushed a tiny `SETUP.md` to my dotfiles with the steps I took. Quick follow-ups: 1) Is it recommended to commit `asdf/.tool-versions` in dotfiles? 2) Any opinion on storing `SSL_CERT_FILE` for corporate proxy certs?

Sana: Yes commit `.tool-versions` — makes CI and teammates consistent. For corporate CA, do NOT commit cert files. Store them in 1Password and add a small `scripts/import-corp-ca.sh` that fetches the cert and sets `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` in your shell env. Add instructions to `SETUP.md`.

devops-bot: Reminder from infra: if you ever accidentally commit secrets, open a ticket with `@security` immediately. We have a revocation and rotation playbook. Also recommended: add `SETUP.example` not real secrets.

Hiro: Thanks everyone, really helpful. I pushed SETUP.md and a minimal `.tool-versions`. Appreciate the quick onboarding help! :tada:

Marcel: Welcome aboard Hiro — ping `#devex` or me if you want pair-setup time.

Sana: Agreed — welcome! If you want a one-hour pairing session to sync dotfiles across machines, ping me.

devops-bot: DevEx checklist: brew, asdf, direnv, 1password-cli, ssh keys, docker (if needed). Docs: https://redwood.ai/devex/bootstrap.
